title: Redwood intro + cost/unit economics for Moraine Energy
summary: Initial discovery covering Moraine's latency and budget constraints, exploration of hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, per-token cost breakdown, batching and KV-cache levers, and pilot scope. Customer to provide traffic patterns and security requirements; Redwood to send pricing scenarios and pilot proposal.
action_items: Evan: export 90/95/99 latency targets and peak QPS by 2026-12-18
Priya: run quick back-of-envelope unit-cost model for their average payload and share by 2026-12-16
Alex: send security checklist and Redwood SOC2 summary by 2026-12-15
next_steps: Redwood to share three pricing scenarios (hosted low-latency, dedicated reserved, private VPC) by 12/16
Moraine to run an internal spike comparing current on-prem throughput to Redwood dedicated profile in early Jan
Schedule pilot scoping session w/ procurement on 2026-12-21
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-14 16:00 UTC - Duration ~68m - Attendees: Alex Mercer, Priya Raman (Redwood); Evan Kline, Sofia Alvarez, Marcus Dwyer (Moraine)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros. I'm Alex, AE on the platform. Priya is our systems SE who will band with me on the tech bits.
00:17 Evan: Hi all, Evan CTO at Moraine. Sofia leads ML infra and Marcus is our SRE. We have a tight budget for next Q and want to understand unit economics for inference.
00:31 Alex: Great. high level we want to understand your success criteria, volume, latency targets and security needs. then we'll map hosted / dedicated / private to cost per call.
00:45 Sofia: Our main use case is real-time anomaly detection on sensor streams, so median latency needs to be under 120ms for 99% of calls, peak bursts up to 6k QPS. Budget is... well, probably under $40k per month for inference initially.
01:05 Priya: ok that helps. bursts and low p99 is the tricky part; we usually talk about batching vs single-token latency, and KV cache for prefix-heavy workloads. can you describe the request size? tokens per request?
01:23 Sofia: Most payloads are short — 40 to 90 tokens per call. sometimes we hit longer context for session history but that is <10% of calls.
01:36 Marcus: question on residency — must data stay in our VPC? we have some regulatory things for raw telemetry.
01:46 Alex: good call. Residency and entanglement with raw telemetry pushes toward Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be OK if you don't send raw PII or if shipping via encrypted proxy and we offer contractual data handling. we'll cover KMS options.
02:02 Evan: can you sketch per-token pricing? like, ballpark hosted vs dedicated?
02:09 Priya: sure, ballpark — hosted per-token is typically higher but no infra overhead. dedicated amortizes GPUs and gives a lower per-token cost at scale but requires commit or reserved capacity. there are also batching and caching levers that can lower cost by 20-70% depending on workload.
02:30 Sofia: that range is huge — 20 to 70% — can you give an example with our 60-token avg?
02:38 Priya: yeah. assume model A runs ~0.6ms/token on our runtime and with continuous batching at your observed batch sizes, you might see a 30% effective token cost reduction. with KV cache for repeated prefix tokens you can cut token invoicing for prefixes by up to 80% in ideal cases. worst case — random unique payloads — minimal caching so closer to the 20% lower bound from batching only.
03:05 Marcus: I'm a little fuzzy — KV cash? do you mean KV cache?
03:09 Sofia: (laughs) yeah KV cache.
03:12 Priya: sorry, yeah kv cache — our transcription sometimes calls it KV cash — helps where a big chunk is shared context like device metadata. then runtime doesn't recompute those tokens per request.
03:25 Evan: and quantization? you support int8/4 options?
03:29 Priya: we have quantization profiles that can drop effective GPU usage and cost without big quality loss for many workloads, depends on your evals. that can be another 10-30% saving in some cases.
03:40 Alex: to make it concrete: for hosted, we price per 1k tokens at X (we'll send scenarios). for dedicated we convert your commit into effective per-token assuming 18 months amortization of GPUs plus ops. private is similar to dedicated but includes customer-managed network & KMS, so there's an infra surcharge.
03:58 Sofia: whoops — can you put some numeric examples in the follow up? hard to make decisions on qualitative percents.
04:04 Alex: absolutely, we'll send three scenarios: low-latency hosted (higher unit price, no commit), dedicated reserved (lower per-token, commit), private (similar unit to dedicated + network/residency surcharge).
04:18 Marcus: SLA question — we need 99.9% on inference for critical pipelines. what does Redwood offer?
04:26 Priya: our Dedicated customers get SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; hosted has standard availability but different tiers. for 99.9% p99 we usually recommend dedicated with tailored autoscaling and fallback models.
04:39 Evan: fallback how?
04:42 Priya: two levers — routing policy that falls back to a cheaper model variant on overload and region fallback. also auto-burst pools for short peaks. we'll need to size the pilot to test that.
04:57 Sofia: security — SOC 2? SSO? KMS/HSM? audit logs?
05:02 Alex: yes SOC2 Type II summary available, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and KMS integrations. Private gives you own KMS. we'll attach security docs.
05:13 Marcus: and network connectivity for private — do you ship an appliance or is it VPC peering?
05:17 Priya: typically VPC peering or private link. for on-prem we have an appliance option but that is heavier.
05:25 Evan: timeline — we may want a pilot in Jan to validate unit economics. can Redwood help with a short pilot that uses a small dedicated pool?
05:32 Alex: yes pilot options: 2-week eval with a small dedicated pool and a pre-flight baseline on hosted. Pilot pricing will show effective per-token at your load and SLOs.
05:42 Sofia: decision factors for us are total monthly cost under $40k, meeting 120ms p99, and compliance boxed — if dedicated gets us to $30k with the target p99 that's attractive.
05:56 Priya: for a quick ROI calc we need peak QPS distribution, token distribution, and percent of repeat prefixes. Evan, can you export those?
06:06 Evan: yes we'll pull logs and send a sampled distribution by Friday.
06:11 Alex: perfect. also helpful — any internal procurement lead or cost owner?
06:15 Evan: procurement is CCed, but our finance lead is Lila Park — she'll join procurement discussions after the pilot.
06:23 Marcus: curious — competitors. we looked at hugging face infra and some self-hosted stacks. concerns are ops overhead and kernel perf on our side.
06:33 Priya: totally. one upside of Redwood is runtime kernel selection and continuous batching tuned for high throughput; less ops work for you.
06:43 Sofia: can you run a quick calc now? like a back-of-envelope per-token given our 60 token average and 2k sustained QPS with 6k bursts?
06:52 Priya: quick math: 2k QPS * 60 tokens * 3600s * 24 = big monthly tokens — but easier: tokens/sec = 120k tokens/sec sustained; that's about 10.3B tokens/day — wait that's off. let me recalibrate — that's 120k tokens/sec * 3600 = 432M tokens/hour; *24 = 10.37B tokens/day indeed, which is huge — maybe I misheard.
07:22 Sofia: oh — I think you multiplied by 24, but our 2k QPS is peak during daylight only, average sustained is 400 QPS overnight. but we'll provide the real histogram.
07:34 Priya: ok with histogram we'll produce a much cleaner model — but in general if sustained at those numbers you definitely move to dedicated. per-token differences could be 2-5x between small hosted usage and amortized dedicated at scale.
07:51 Evan: risk — we can't sign big multi-year commit without seeing a pilot. can Redwood offer short commit or an options-based ramp?
07:59 Alex: yes we can do pilot-first with a short reserved window and then convert pilots to longer commit if numbers match. we also support burst credits to avoid up-front capacity risk.
08:11 Marcus: any gotchas around latency when batching? we can't add 100ms wait windows.
08:17 Priya: we use latency-aware continuous batching — we set a max latency threshold and flush; batching gains occur without adding noticeable tail latency if configured carefully. for strict <120ms p99 we might limit batch sizes and rely more on higher tier GPU and dedicated pools.
08:36 Sofia: are you able to instrument token-level billing per route? we need per-model and per-feature granularity.
08:43 Alex: yes console has per-route token breakdowns, and we can expose token-level logs for your SRE to ingest.
08:50 Evan: ok let's wrap. any final questions?
08:54 Sofia: just want to ensure the follow up includes numeric scenarios and a pilot scope doc.
08:58 Alex: will do. recap: Moraine to send traffic histograms, eviction rate of prefixes, and latency targets. Redwood to send pricing scenarios, SOC2, security checklist, and pilot proposal. schedule pilot scoping on 12/21 with procurement.
09:15 Evan: thanks all. good session.
09:20 Alex: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-heard words; we've kept speaker labels mostly accurate but Fireflies occasionally tags generics.
additional_notes: Customer emphasized budget cap of $40k/mo and strict p99 <120ms. Will provide traffic histograms and prefix repetition stats. Redwood to prepare numeric per-token scenarios and pilot SOW.
